maria: Quick sync — proposal to decompose the console auth chokepoint into a lightweight prefilter (fast allow/deny using token cache) + authoritative postfilter on the projection layer. Pros: p95 drops, easier short-circuiting. Cons: duplication of policy logic, more cache invalidation complexity. Thoughts?

alex: +1 on split for latency-sensitive routes. How do we keep consistency for newly minted grants? cache TTL won't cut it.

jyoti: Could we use a short-lived change-log stream to invalidate per-tenant cache keys? small metadata update messages from auth svc.

sam: Concern: postfilter adds CPU on the projection path — might affect heavy dashboards. Need perf numbers. Can we push partial deny (mask fields) rather than full abort?

henry: For rollouts, propose an opt-in canary where prefilter is authoritative for 10% requests and we log diffs. Use routing metadata: header X-Auth-Mode:pre-canary

maria: nice. Also thinking about RBAC pushdown: translate role -> allowed_projection_mask at model-compile time and store in proto. That avoids re-eval on each request.

alex: Implementation note: store masks in redis with a versioned key like auth-mask:v2:{tenant}. Invalidate on rolechange event.

jyoti: telemetry: track metric auth_diff{route,tenant,pre_allowed,post_allowed}. Use this to detect policy drift during canary.

sam: ops question: what SLO impact if prefilter fails? fallback should be postfilter; add metric auth_prefilter_fail_rate and circuit breaker to disable prefilter.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: auth-prefilter-service -> staging (build 0.8.3) by ci-pipeline at 2024-11-14T09:01:12Z :rocket:

maria: ok next steps: sketch implementation (alex + jyoti), integration test plan (sam), canary plan (henry). I'll update RFC with these items and a small perf benchmark target (p95 reduction target 20%).
